front_blocks.md: Define **operating system**.

back_blocks.md: An operating system is software that provides an **interface between the user and the hardware** in a computer system.

cards.front_md: Define **operating system**.
cards.back_md: An operating system is software that provides an **interface between the user and the hardware** in a computer system.

front_blocks.md: What does an operating system hide from the user?

back_blocks.md: An operating system hides the **complexities of the hardware** from the user, so a user does not need to know where on secondary storage data is kept.

cards.front_md: What does an operating system hide from the user?

front_blocks.md: Define **user interface**.

back_blocks.md: A user interface is **how the user interacts with the operating system**.

cards.front_md: Define **user interface**.
cards.back_md: A user interface is **how the user interacts with the operating system**.

front_blocks.md: Name the four types of user interface.

back_blocks.md: The four types of user interface are **command line interface (CLI)**, **graphical user interface (GUI)**, **menu** and **natural language interface (NLI)**.

cards.front_md: Name the four types of user interface.
cards.back_md: The four types of user interface are **command line interface (CLI)**, **graphical user interface (GUI)**, **menu** and **natural language interface (NLI)**.

front_blocks.md: How does a user interact with a command line interface (CLI)?

back_blocks.md: A user interacts with a command line interface using **text-based commands**.

cards.front_md: How does a user interact with a command line interface (CLI)?
cards.back_md: A user interacts with a command line interface using **text-based commands**.

front_blocks.md: What does WIMP stand for in a graphical user interface?

front_blocks.md: Name the five key management tasks of an operating system.

back_blocks.md: The five key management tasks are **memory management**, **file management**, **security management**, **hardware management** and **process management**.

cards.front_md: Name the five key management tasks of an operating system.
cards.back_md: The five key management tasks are **memory management**, **file management**, **security management**, **hardware management** and **process management**.

front_blocks.md: Define **memory management**.

back_blocks.md: Memory management is the operating system **allocating main memory (RAM) between different programs that are open at the same time**.

cards.front_md: Define **memory management**.
cards.back_md: Memory management is the operating system **allocating main memory (RAM) between different programs that are open at the same time**.

front_blocks.md: Which operating system management task makes multitasking possible?

back_blocks.md: **Memory management** makes multitasking possible, because it prevents data from different programs overwriting each other in RAM.

cards.front_md: Which operating system management task makes multitasking possible?
cards.back_md: **Memory management** makes multitasking possible, because it prevents data from different programs overwriting each other in RAM.

front_blocks.md: Define **file management**.

back_blocks.md: File management is the operating system **creating, organising, manipulating and accessing files and folders** on a computer system.

cards.front_md: Define **file management**.
cards.back_md: File management is the operating system **creating, organising, manipulating and accessing files and folders** on a computer system.

front_blocks.md: What do permissions allow the operating system to control?

back_blocks.md: Permissions allow the operating system to control **who can access, modify and delete files and folders**.

cards.front_md: What do permissions allow the operating system to control?
cards.back_md: Permissions allow the operating system to control **who can access, modify and delete files and folders**.

front_blocks.md: Security management includes password-protected system accounts, a firewall, virus scanning and file <u>**                    **</u>.

back_blocks.md: Security management includes password-protected system accounts, a firewall, virus scanning and file **encryption**.

cards.front_md: Security management includes password-protected system accounts, a firewall, virus scanning and file <u>**                    **</u>.
cards.back_md: Security management includes password-protected system accounts, a firewall, virus scanning and file **encryption**.

front_blocks.md: Define **device driver**.

back_blocks.md: A device driver is **a piece of software used to control a piece of hardware**.

cards.front_md: Define **device driver**.
cards.back_md: A device driver is **a piece of software used to control a piece of hardware**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The same device driver will work on any operating system.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Device drivers are **operating system specific** and are regularly updated.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The same device driver will work on any operating system.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Device drivers are **operating system specific** and are regularly updated.

front_blocks.md: What is plug-and-play (PnP)?

back_blocks.md: Plug-and-play is the operating system **automatically detecting and configuring new peripherals** without manually installing device drivers or power cycling the system.

cards.front_md: What is plug-and-play (PnP)?
cards.back_md: Plug-and-play is the operating system **automatically detecting and configuring new peripherals** without manually installing device drivers or power cycling the system.

front_blocks.md: Define **time slicing**.

back_blocks.md: Time slicing is the operating system **dividing processor time into small chunks and allocating them to different processes**.

cards.front_md: Define **time slicing**.
cards.back_md: Time slicing is the operating system **dividing processor time into small chunks and allocating them to different processes**.

front_blocks.md: What does an operating system use to decide which process is executed next?

back_blocks.md: An operating system uses a **scheduling algorithm** to prioritise processes and decide which is executed next.

cards.front_md: What does an operating system use to decide which process is executed next?
cards.back_md: An operating system uses a **scheduling algorithm** to prioritise processes and decide which is executed next.

front_blocks.md: Define **utility software**.

back_blocks.md: Utility software is a **collection of tools designed to help maintain a computer system**.

cards.front_md: Define **utility software**.
cards.back_md: Utility software is a **collection of tools designed to help maintain a computer system**.

front_blocks.md: Name four examples of utility software.

back_blocks.md: Examples of utility software include a **disk formatter**, a **virus checker**, **defragmentation software**, **disk contents analysis / disk repair software**, **file compression** and **back-up software**.

cards.front_md: Name four examples of utility software.
cards.back_md: Examples of utility software include a **disk formatter**, a **virus checker**, **defragmentation software**, **disk contents analysis / disk repair software**, **file compression** and **back-up software**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Utility software is designed to perform a wide range of tasks.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Utility software is designed to perform a **limited number of tasks**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Utility software is designed to perform a wide range of tasks.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Utility software is designed to perform a **limited number of tasks**.

front_blocks.md: What does utility software interact with directly?

back_blocks.md: Utility software interacts with the computer's **hardware**, for example secondary storage devices.

cards.front_md: What does utility software interact with directly?
cards.back_md: Utility software interacts with the computer's **hardware**, for example secondary storage devices.

front_blocks.md: What does a disk formatter do?

back_blocks.md: A disk formatter **prepares a storage device for use** by **creating a file system** and **organising the space into sectors and tracks**.

cards.front_md: What does a disk formatter do?
cards.back_md: A disk formatter **prepares a storage device for use** by **creating a file system** and **organising the space into sectors and tracks**.

front_blocks.md: Give one reason a disk would need to be formatted.

back_blocks.md: A disk is formatted to **wipe and re-initialise** it, to **change the file system format** or to **remove all data and errors** before installing a new operating system.

cards.front_md: Give one reason a disk would need to be formatted.
cards.back_md: A disk is formatted to **wipe and re-initialise** it, to **change the file system format** or to **remove all data and errors** before installing a new operating system.

front_blocks.md: What does a virus checker scan?

back_blocks.md: A virus checker scans **email attachments**, **websites** and **downloaded files** to search for issues.

cards.front_md: What does a virus checker scan?
cards.back_md: A virus checker scans **email attachments**, **websites** and **downloaded files** to search for issues.

front_blocks.md: Name the two ways a virus checker can identify malware.

back_blocks.md: A virus checker can use a list of known **unique malware fingerprints (signatures)**, or **monitor the behaviour of programs** to identify suspicious activity.

cards.front_md: Name the two ways a virus checker can identify malware.
cards.back_md: A virus checker can use a list of known **unique malware fingerprints (signatures)**, or **monitor the behaviour of programs** to identify suspicious activity.

front_blocks.md: Virus checkers check for updates so that the database of <u>**                    **</u> stays up to date.

back_blocks.md: Virus checkers check for updates so that the database of **signatures** stays up to date.

cards.front_md: Virus checkers check for updates so that the database of <u>**                    **</u> stays up to date.
cards.back_md: Virus checkers check for updates so that the database of **signatures** stays up to date.

front_blocks.md: Define **defragmentation software**.

back_blocks.md: Defragmentation software **groups fragmented files back together** in order to **improve the access speed** of a hard disk drive.

cards.front_md: Define **defragmentation software**.
cards.back_md: Defragmentation software **groups fragmented files back together** in order to **improve the access speed** of a hard disk drive.

front_blocks.md: Why does data on a hard disk drive become fragmented?

back_blocks.md: As files are deleted they **leave gaps**, and as new programs and data are added **these gaps get filled**, so data becomes fragmented.

cards.front_md: Why does data on a hard disk drive become fragmented?
cards.back_md: As files are deleted they **leave gaps**, and as new programs and data are added **these gaps get filled**, so data becomes fragmented.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Defragmentation software can be used on any type of secondary storage.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Defragmentation can only be used on **magnetic storage**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Defragmentation software can be used on any type of secondary storage.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Defragmentation can only be used on **magnetic storage**.

front_blocks.md: What does disk contents analysis / disk repair software check?

back_blocks.md: It checks the **structure and health of a disk**, including files, folders, sectors and the file allocation table.

cards.front_md: What does disk contents analysis / disk repair software check?
cards.back_md: It checks the **structure and health of a disk**, including files, folders, sectors and the file allocation table.

front_blocks.md: Give one task that disk repair software performs.

back_blocks.md: Disk repair software **diagnoses and fixes errors** such as bad sectors and file system corruption, and can **recover lost or damaged files**.

cards.front_md: Give one task that disk repair software performs.
cards.back_md: Disk repair software **diagnoses and fixes errors** such as bad sectors and file system corruption, and can **recover lost or damaged files**.

front_blocks.md: Define **file compression**.

back_blocks.md: File compression **reduces the amount of secondary storage required** by performing an algorithm on the original data.

cards.front_md: Define **file compression**.
cards.back_md: File compression **reduces the amount of secondary storage required** by performing an algorithm on the original data.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between lossy and lossless compression?

back_blocks.md: **Lossy** compression **removes data**, so the original file **cannot be re-created**. **Lossless** compression **orders data more efficiently**, so the original file **can be re-created**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between lossy and lossless compression?
cards.back_md: **Lossy** compression **removes data**, so the original file **cannot be re-created**. **Lossless** compression **orders data more efficiently**, so the original file **can be re-created**.

front_blocks.md: Why is back-up software used?

back_blocks.md: Back-up software **creates copies of personal data** to keep it safe in the event of **accidental loss** or **data theft**.

cards.front_md: Why is back-up software used?
cards.back_md: Back-up software **creates copies of personal data** to keep it safe in the event of **accidental loss** or **data theft**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a full backup and an incremental backup?

back_blocks.md: A **full** backup copies **all files**, which is safest but slow. An **incremental** backup copies **only files added or modified since the last backup**, which is faster but less secure.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a full backup and an incremental backup?
cards.back_md: A **full** backup copies **all files**, which is safest but slow. An **incremental** backup copies **only files added or modified since the last backup**, which is faster but less secure.

front_blocks.md: Backups can be scheduled to run at less busy periods of the day so they do not take up valuable <u>**            **</u> resources.

back_blocks.md: Backups can be scheduled to run at less busy periods of the day so they do not take up valuable **system** resources.

cards.front_md: Backups can be scheduled to run at less busy periods of the day so they do not take up valuable <u>**            **</u> resources.
cards.back_md: Backups can be scheduled to run at less busy periods of the day so they do not take up valuable **system** resources.

front_blocks.md: Define **program library**.

back_blocks.md: A program library is a **collection of pre-written code**, called **library routines**, that programmers can **reuse** in their own software.

cards.front_md: Define **program library**.
cards.back_md: A program library is a **collection of pre-written code**, called **library routines**, that programmers can **reuse** in their own software.

front_blocks.md: Name two common tasks that library routines can perform.

back_blocks.md: Library routines can perform common tasks such as **sorting**, **displaying graphics**, **playing sounds** and **managing data**.

cards.front_md: Name two common tasks that library routines can perform.
cards.back_md: Library routines can perform common tasks such as **sorting**, **displaying graphics**, **playing sounds** and **managing data**.

front_blocks.md: How does using a program library save development time?

back_blocks.md: **Pre-written routines can be reused**, so programmers do not need to write common functions from scratch.

cards.front_md: How does using a program library save development time?
cards.back_md: **Pre-written routines can be reused**, so programmers do not need to write common functions from scratch.

front_blocks.md: Why does using a program library improve reliability?

back_blocks.md: Library routines are usually **thoroughly tested and debugged**, which reduces the chance of errors.

cards.front_md: Why does using a program library improve reliability?
cards.back_md: Library routines are usually **thoroughly tested and debugged**, which reduces the chance of errors.

front_blocks.md: How does a program library promote standardisation?

back_blocks.md: A program library promotes **consistency in how common tasks are implemented**, such as file handling and sorting.

cards.front_md: How does a program library promote standardisation?
cards.back_md: A program library promotes **consistency in how common tasks are implemented**, such as file handling and sorting.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Using a program library increases the duplication of code across programs.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A program library **promotes code reuse**, because well-tested routines can be used in multiple programs, **reducing duplication**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Using a program library increases the duplication of code across programs.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A program library **promotes code reuse**, because well-tested routines can be used in multiple programs, **reducing duplication**.

front_blocks.md: Define **dynamic link library (DLL)**.

back_blocks.md: A dynamic link library is a **file containing pre-written code**, such as functions or routines, that can be **used by multiple programs at runtime**.

cards.front_md: Define **dynamic link library (DLL)**.
cards.back_md: A dynamic link library is a **file containing pre-written code**, such as functions or routines, that can be **used by multiple programs at runtime**.

front_blocks.md: When is a DLL loaded into memory?

back_blocks.md: A DLL is only loaded **when it is needed at runtime**, which saves system resources.

cards.front_md: When is a DLL loaded into memory?
cards.back_md: A DLL is only loaded **when it is needed at runtime**, which saves system resources.

front_blocks.md: How does using a DLL reduce program size?

back_blocks.md: A DLL **keeps reusable code separate** from the program, so the program itself is smaller.

cards.front_md: How does using a DLL reduce program size?
cards.back_md: A DLL **keeps reusable code separate** from the program, so the program itself is smaller.

front_blocks.md: Why does using a DLL make maintenance easier?

back_blocks.md: A DLL only needs to be **updated once**, and every program that uses it benefits from the update.

cards.front_md: Why does using a DLL make maintenance easier?
cards.back_md: A DLL only needs to be **updated once**, and every program that uses it benefits from the update.

front_blocks.md: DLLs save memory because they can be <u>**            **</u> between programs.

back_blocks.md: DLLs save memory because they can be **shared** between programs.

cards.front_md: DLLs save memory because they can be <u>**            **</u> between programs.
cards.back_md: DLLs save memory because they can be **shared** between programs.

front_blocks.md: Give one disadvantage of using a DLL.

back_blocks.md: A program may **fail to run if a required DLL is missing**, newer DLLs can cause **version conflicts**, altered DLLs can pose **security risks**, and errors inside a DLL can be **hard to trace** across multiple programs.

cards.front_md: Give one disadvantage of using a DLL.
cards.back_md: A program may **fail to run if a required DLL is missing**, newer DLLs can cause **version conflicts**, altered DLLs can pose **security risks**, and errors inside a DLL can be **hard to trace** across multiple programs.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Updating a DLL can stop a program that uses it from working.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Newer DLLs that are not compatible can cause **version conflicts**.
